title: Centralize observability log routing and enrichment pipeline
creator: Asha Menon
description: Objective: Build a single, maintainable log ingestion and routing pipeline that centralizes structured log validation, correlation-id enrichment and fan-out to both Loki (fast-lookup/dev tooling) and an ELK stack (long-term analytics and BI). Background: We've accumulated multiple ingestion paths (legacy syslog, fluent-bit agents, and ad-hoc service-side emitters). This increases cognitive load for on-call, fractures schemas, and makes tracing correlation brittle. This ticket implements an ingestion gateway + enrichment layer that standardizes envelopes, performs schema validation, injects trace/correlation ids when missing, tags environment/tenant, and applies retention/route policies. The gateway will also expose backpressure metrics and a health API to coordinate rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: All service logs can be routed through the gateway with no more than 5ms median extra latency at p50
Gateway performs JSON schema validation and drops/metrics-invalid logs with a distinct metric and sample stored for debugging
Trace and correlation IDs are present for 99.9% of application logs after enrichment for instrumented services
Fan-out configuration routes dev and staging traffic to Loki and prod to ELK+S3 for retention according to policy
Dashboard tiles in Console show ingestion rate, validation failure rate, per-tenant throughput, and alert on sustained queueing/backpressure
Rollout plan for incremental adoption with canary and automatic fallback to existing ingest paths
plan: Phase 1: PoC gateway using Fluent Bit + lightweight enrichment plugin behind a TLS Ingress (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Replace PoC plugin with a small Go microservice (gateway) that supports schema registry lookups and KV caching for fast enrichment (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Integration tests + canary rollout for 10% of traffic, instrument dashboards and alerts (1 week)
Phase 4: Full rollout, decommission legacy collectors and publish migration guides for SDKs and services (2 weeks)
Post-rollout: Add retention mapping UI to Console and automate cold storage lifecycle transitions
decisions: Use a custom Go gateway instead of upstream-only Fluentd to keep enrichment logic and schema evolution under source control — trade-off: increased maintenance cost vs. better control and observability
Persist samples of validation failures to a bounded S3 bucket for forensic debugging rather than sending all failures to ELK to avoid noise/cost
Route low-volume developer namespaces to Loki for fast tail logs; route high-volume production namespaces to ELK + partitioned S3 for long-term analytics
Enrichment will prefer service-injected trace ids; gateway will only synthesize trace/correlation id when missing and record a synthetic flag to avoid confusion in downstream telemetry

notes: Migration: provide a sidecar mode for services that cannot route through the network gateway immediately
Testing: create an end-to-end scenario that verifies trace-id continuity from HTTP ingress -> service emit -> gateway enrichment -> Loki/ELK search
Observability: emit metrics 'ingest.total', 'ingest.validated', 'ingest.invalid', 'ingest.enriched.synthetic_trace' with tenant tags
Policy: default retention mapping: dev=7d (Loki), staging=30d (Loki+ELK), prod=90d (ELK+S3 archive) — configurable per tenant
Backpressure: gateway exposes queue_depth Prometheus metric and will shed non-critical debug logs when queue depth > threshold to protect customer-facing traces
